copy.title: Top 22 UK Seed-Stage Regional Fintech Companies
copy.h1: Top 22 UK Seed-Stage Regional Fintech Companies Ranked by Total Raised
copy.metaDescription: See the top 22 UK seed-stage regional fintech companies ranked by total raised, with funding spread, locations and what each company builds.
intro: This page ranks 22 regional fintech companies in the UK seed stage by total raised. The companies together have raised £117.7m.
The ranking shows where the funding sits, which regions the companies are based in, and what the leading companies do.

sections.heading: How the seed-stage fintech funding is spread
paragraphs: The median total raised is £3.3m, while the mean is £5.3m. The mean sits above the median because TreeCard, which ranks first with £23.7m, raised far more than the others.
Eight of the 22 companies have at least £5m, and 2 of the 22 have at least £10m. The top 6 hold 56.5% of the combined total, which is £66.4m.

sections.heading: Where the regional fintech companies are based
paragraphs: The North West has the largest group of companies in this dataset, with 6 companies (27.3%) and £24.6m combined. The South West follows with 5 companies (22.7%) and £49.9m combined.
The East of England has 3 companies (13.6%) and £17.1m combined, while the East of Scotland has 2 companies (9.1%) and £4.5m combined.

sections.heading: Team sizes among the top UK fintech companies
paragraphs: Most of the companies, 12 of 22, have 10 to 24 employees, and they hold £85m combined. The 5 to 9 employee group has 7 companies with £20.5m combined.
Fewer companies sit at the extremes. One company has fewer than 5 employees, and one has 50 to 99 employees.

sections.heading: What the leading companies build
paragraphs: TreeCard develops wooden bank cards and a mobile app that helps users track their spending, and it uses surcharge profits to fund reforestation programmes. Clove Group develops technology for broadening access to financial advice.
multifi provides small and medium businesses with flexible credit limits, and Penny develops a mobile app that finds users' different pension pots and transfers and displays them in one place.
